## About
Jeff's life in wheel alignment started at a chain shop. After many years of slowly gathering equipment and building a client base, he opened a little shop of his own. Today he's at 632 11th Avenue So. in Hopkins.
He works on humble taxis and commuter cars as well as Ferrari and Lotus. He uses a Hunter alignment computer, and he can also put a vehicle straight with hand tools. His pricing is set similar to the chain shops, but nobody's pushing him to rush and cut corners.
Jeff works alone, so everything is by appointment. He may growl and bark, but he's never actually bitten anyone. The shop holds a 4.9 rating from 202 Google reviews.

## Services
- Computerized wheel alignments: Done on a Hunter camera system. Jeff can align to factory specs or custom settings.
- Tire service and some sales: Mounting on a Hunter "tulip" style changer with all plastic tool surfaces. Bought your tires online? Bring them in.
- Wheel balancing: On a FMC/John Bean computer balancer with "finger plates" to improve centering of wheels on the machine.
- Suspension and steering part service: Strut and bushing/bearing press work, including ball joints, tie rod ends and drive axles.
- Brake reline and rotor/drum machine service: Brake relines and rotor and drum machining. No ABS service at this time.
- Corner weight adjustments: Measured with Longacre digital scales.
- Motorcycle work: Some motorcycle work using the Hunter machine and a static balancer.

## FAQ
Q: Do I need an appointment?
A: Yes. Jeff works alone, so all work is by appointment to keep his day full and your wait shorter.

Q: How far out are you booked?
A: Usually a few days to a week, so call ahead.

Q: Can I bring tires I bought online?
A: Yes. Tire Rack, Discount and other mail order buyers are welcome.

Q: When's the last car in?
A: Usually around 5:00 during the week and 4:00 on Saturday.

Q: Do you do ABS work?
A: Not right now. Jeff doesn't own a scan tool, so ABS service is off the list for the time being.
